title: The Unity of the Church
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The unity of the church is the spiritual oneness of God’s people in one Lord, one faith, one Spirit, one body, and one Gospel. This unity is received in Christ and must be protected in love, truth, humility, and peace.
summary: The unity of the church is the spiritual oneness of God’s people in one Lord, one faith, one Spirit, one body, and one Gospel. This unity is received in Christ and must be protected in love, truth, humility, and peace.
christFocus: Jesus Christ creates the church’s unity by reconciling sinners to God and to one another through His cross. He is the Lord who gathers divided people into one body.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The church’s unity is not based on personality, preference, culture, politics, music style, background, or human sameness. It is grounded in God Himself: one Spirit, one Lord, one Father, one faith, one baptism, and one hope.

Christ makes peace through His cross. He tears down hostility and brings formerly divided people near to God and to one another. Gospel unity is therefore deeper than natural similarity.

Unity must be protected. Believers are commanded to walk with humility, gentleness, patience, bearing with one another in love, and maintaining the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

Biblical unity does not require ignoring truth or tolerating false doctrine. The church’s unity is unity in Christ, in the Gospel, and in the truth God has spoken.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Division can quickly damage a church’s witness and wound believers. Pride, preferences, gossip, bitterness, and party spirit can make Christ’s body look like the world.

This doctrine calls believers to a better way. Unity does not mean everyone is identical; it means diverse people are held together by Christ and learn to love one another under His lordship.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Protect the unity of the church with humility and truth. Refuse gossip, pride, bitterness, and unnecessary division. Pursue peace without compromising the Gospel, and remember that Christ shed His blood to make one people for Himself.
